headline: Brown, Maxey and James combine for 78 points in 76ers' 127-121 win over Bulls
text: CHICAGO -- — Jaylen Brown scored 29 points, Tyrese Maxey added 27 and LeBron James had his highest-scoring effort so far in a Philadelphia uniform as the 76ers held off the struggling Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday afternoon. James had a season-high 22 for the 76ers, who got 18 points and 10 rebounds from Joel Embiid and 13 points from VJ Edgecombe . At 9-2, the 76ers — the Eastern Conference leaders — are off to their best 11-game start since going 10-1 to open the 2000-01 season. Josh Giddey had 19 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds for Chicago. Matas Buzelis added 19 points for the Bulls, who got 18 from Caleb Wilson , 17 from Jalen Smith , 12 from Isaac Okoro and 10 from Noa Essengue . The Bulls dropped their seventh straight and fell to 1-8, tying the third-worst nine-game start in team history. Chicago started 0-9 was in 1967-68 — the franchise’s second season — and 2004-05. James' 3-pointer 3:15 into the game gave him 1,897 career points against Chicago, making him the all-time leading scorer against the Bulls. Abdul-Jabbar — who was the NBA's all-time leading scorer, until James passed him for the No. 1 spot in 2023 — scored 1,895 points against the Bulls in 76 games; James was playing a regular season game against Chicago for the 70th time. Brown made 11 of 22 shots from the floor in his final game before facing his former team — the Boston Celtics — in a real game for the first time. The teams met in the preseason, making the first time Brown went up against the team that traded him to Philadelphia this past offseason, but Tuesday's game in Philadelphia will be the first time Brown faces the Celtics in a game that counts in the standings. Up next 76ers: Host Boston on Tuesday. Bulls: Host San Antonio on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Austin Reaves steps in for Luka Donic with 43 points in Lakers win over Pistons
text: DETROIT -- — Austin Reaves thought he had a very fortunate night against the Detroit Pistons . He was the only one in the Los Angeles Lakers locker room who thought so. On a night when the Lakers were playing without red-hot Luka Doncic , Reaves scored 43 points against one of the league's best defenses in a 121-116 win. “I was a lucky basketball player tonight,” said Reaves, who went 14 of 27 from the floor, including 4 of 6 on 3-pointers, and added a perfect 11-for-11 from the free-throw line. Walker Kessler , who finished with 12 points and 16 rebounds, disagreed with his teammate. “Luka is an incredible player, and I think there are times when he's playing that A.R. kind of has to take a secondary role,” he said. "But you could see tonight that he's a very capable player. “It doesn't matter if we get a Luka game or an A.R. game — we're still going to win.” Reaves had big shoes to fill, as the Lakers needed him to step up in place of the league's hottest player. In his last four games, all Los Angeles wins, Donic was averaging 45 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. That's a tough scoreline to match, but the 28-year-old came close. He had five rebounds and four assists in 36:41 with only one turnover. “He’s a heck of a playmaker, a heck of a scorer, and a great competitor,” Kessler said. “It's just incredible to play alongside he and Luka, because they hit some really, really tough shots.” He saved his toughest for last. The Pistons trailed by 26 points in the second quarter but were only down 109-104 going into the final minute. The Lakers couldn't get into their offense, and Reaves ended up with the ball as the shot clock was about to expire. He flipped up a one-legged, off-balance 3-pointer that went through the net to erase Detroit's last chance. “That was a terrible shot.” he said. "When I stepped back to shoot, I thought it looked like one of those ridiculous shots that Luka makes. I didn't even try to make it, and then it went in. “Now that looks like a good shot in the box score, but it was 100% lucky.” Reaves quite often points to luck and good fortune when talking about himself, but that underrates the work he's put into just having an NBA career. After playing two years at Wichita State and a year at Oklahoma, he declared for the 2021 draft. He went undrafted, but only because that's what he wanted. The Pistons, victims of his big night on Sunday, were planning to pick him with the 42nd pick, but he declined in order to sign as a free agent with the Lakers. The Pistons ended up taking Isaiah Livers, who played 130 NBA games and is now playing in Japan. Meanwhile, Reaves came into the game averaging 23.0 points per game during Doncic's four-game hot streak, then found another gear against the team he shunned. “There's never a dull moment around here,” he joked. “The good thing is that I didn't play a perfect game tonight. There's always room to get better.” ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Dosunmu, Ball lead Timberwolves past slumping Jazz, 115-100
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points and LaMelo Ball added 24 points and five assists to help the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Utah Jazz 115-100 on Sunday night. Jaden McDaniels finished with 16 points, Bones Hyland had 14 off the bench, and Rudy Gobert chipped in 10 points and 15 rebounds for the Wolves (8-3), who have won four in a row and are 5-2 without Anthony Edwards . The All-Star guard is expected to miss two months after undergoing knee surgery Oct. 29. Darryn Peterson led the Jazz with 26 points and six rebounds. Keyonte George scored 19 points in three quarters before missing the fourth quarter with a sprained right ankle. After splitting their first two games of the season, the Jazz have lost eight in a row and sit at the bottom of the Western Conference. They played Sunday without forward Lauri Markkanen (right wrist), who hit eight 3-pointers in a loss at Dallas on Friday night. Ball brought the crowd to its feet when he made a steal at midcourt and cruised to an uncontested dunk, giving Minnesota a 70-63 lead midway through the third quarter. Hyland then checked in and scored seven quick points as the Timberwolves ended the third quarter with their biggest lead at 90-72. Utah began the fourth quarter 0 for 9 from the floor and was held scoreless for almost four minutes as Minnesota built its lead to as much as 19 points. The Timberwolves entered the game with the worst free-throw percentage in the league at .648, but they made 27 of 32 from the line Sunday, with Dosunmu going 8 for 8. The game kicked off a season-long eight-game homestand for the Timberwolves. They won’t play a game outside Target Center until the day before Thanksgiving. Up next Jazz: Host Miami on Tuesday night. Timberwolves: Host Dallas on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cooper Flagg has 25 points, career-best 12 assists as Mavericks beat Nets 130-93
text: DALLAS -- — Cooper Flagg had 25 points and a career-high 12 assists for his third consecutive double-double and fourth of the season as the Dallas Mavericks beat the Brooklyn Nets 130-93 on Sunday night. Kyrie Irving scored 21 points and Daniel Gafford added 18 as the Mavericks played the first of a home back-to-back. Michael Porter Jr . had 19 points and nine rebounds for the Nets, who were swept in a back-to-back to begin a four-game road trip. Nolan Traore added 14 points. The Nets didn’t trail until the final two minutes of Saturday’s 124-121 loss at Atlanta but never led against the Mavericks. Flagg, last season’s Rookie of the Year, had his 16th career 20-point half and first this season after opening hot by hitting 5 of 6 shots in the first period. He had missed 6 of 8 shots and scored four points in the first half on Friday against Utah but finished with 21 points in Dallas’ 112-100 win . The Mavericks shot a season best 57.1% and scored a season high in points on Sunday. They led 66-46 at halftime, and the 37-point final margin was the largest of the game. Brooklyn’s Julius Randle grew up in the Dallas area and went into play averaging 23.5 points in his homecoming games but finished with 13 points. Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr ., who tied his career-high with 18 points on Saturday, sat out, not yet cleared for back-to-backs as he recovers from a back injury that limited him to 21 games last season for Louisville. Up next Nets: Visit New Orleans on Wednesday night. Mavericks: Host Indiana on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Paul George and Jayson Tatum lead Celtics to a 117-97 victory over the Bucks
text: MILWAUKEE -- — Paul George scored 27 points, Jayson Tatum added 21 and the Boston Celtics rolled to a 117-97 victory over the slumping Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night. This marked the second matchup between these teams in five nights. The Celtics had beaten the Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday in Boston while resting Tatum. Boston (8-2) built a big enough lead Sunday to sit Tatum for the entire fourth quarter as the Celtics continued a four-game trip that started with a 119-80 win at Charlotte on Friday. The Celtics next head to Philadelphia and Toronto. Kyle Kuzma led Milwaukee with 27 points. Myles Turner scored just three points for the Bucks, though he did have five rebounds and a career-high seven assists. Turner, who has shot 1 of 15 over his last two games, was coming off a scoreless performance in a 121-107 NBA Cup loss to the Toronto Raptors on Frieday. The Bucks (1-9) are off to their worst start since 1993-94, when they lost 10 of their first 11 games and went on to finish 20-62. Kuzma scored 14 points in the first five minutes of the game to help Milwaukee grab an early 20-6 lead. Tatum and George sparked an 18-0 run that enabled the Celtics to take control later in the first half. Tatum scored the final 10 points of the first quarter to cut Milwaukee’s lead to 27-25. George delivered the first eight points of the second period. George’s 3-pointer in the opening minute of the second quarter gave Boston its first lead at 28-27. George then hit a layup and another 3-pointer to cap the 18-0 spurt. Boston owned a 58-45 halftime advantage. The Celtics scored the first nine points of the third period to extend their lead to 22, and they stayed in front by at least 15 the rest of the way. Up next Celtics: At Philadelphia on Tuesday night. Bucks: At New York on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Clippers beat Pelicans to end 7-game losing streak
text: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night. Gradey Dick and rookie Keaton Wagler each scored 15 points and Rui Hachimura added 14 as the Clippers won for the first time since getting past the Sacramento Kings in the season opener. The Clippers went on a 15-6 run to open the fourth quarter to take control with a 117-101 lead and finished off the victory after failing to hold on to double-digit fourth-quarter leads in their previous two games. Trey Murphy III scored 26 points, while Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each added 25 as the Pelicans lost their second consecutive game following a four-game winning streak. Saddiq Bey had 13 points for New Orleans, which was playing the opener of a two-game California trip. The Pelicans shot 50.6% from the floor while getting held to 52 points in the paint after entering the with 61.6 per game in that department to lead the NBA. The Clippers took a 124-107 lead with 4:56 remaining on three free throws from Garland and cruised to the victory from there with a season high in points. Los Angeles shot a season-best 54.8% from the floor. The Clippers led 67-60 at halftime after shooting 52.3% from the floor and getting 14 points from Garland, while Williamson had 17 points for the Pelicans. New Orleans opened the second half on an 18-10 run to take their first lead since the opening minute at 78-77. Los Angeles was without center Isaiah Jackson (groin), as well as former Pelicans star Brandon Ingram (heel), who is close to his debut for his new team. Up next Pelicans: At Golden State on Monday night. Clippers: At Phoenix on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 29 points to lead the Heat to a 114-108 win over the struggling Kings
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 14 rebounds, and three assists in the Miami Heat’s 114-108 win over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday. Antetokounmpo made 14 of 23 shots from the field and added three assists and two blocks. Klay Thompson had 23 points, including seven 3-pointers, for the Heat (4-6), and Bam Adebayo added 18 points and eight rebounds. Darius Acuff Jr . had 32 points and 10 assists for the Kings (1-9), who have not won a home game. The game was tied at 55-all until the Heat went on a 13-4 run, capped by two free throws by Adebayo at the 55-second mark of the second quarter. The Heat led 68-59 at the half. Adebayo, Antetokounmpo, and Davion Mitchell combined for 41 of the Heat’s first-half points. The Heat got the lead up to 16 points in the third quarter, before the Kings surged back to tie the game at 95 on two free throws by De’Andre Hunter at the 6:12 mark of the fourth. The Heat regained the lead and outscored the Kings 19-13 the rest of the way for the victory. Domantas Sabonis did not play for the Kings due to left knee soreness. The Kings announced that the team traded second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder . In return, the Kings received Utah’s 2028 second-round draft pick and Minnesota’s 2030 second-round draft pick. Clifford was selected in the first round (24th overall pick) of the 2025 NBA draft by the Thunder, who traded his draft rights to the Kings. Up next Kings: Host Orlando on Tuesday night. Heat: At Utah on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
